title: Journify Raises $12M Series A Amid 5x Growth
summary: Investors back Journify’s push into the US and Europe Journify , the ad signal infrastructure company, today announced a $12 million Series A at four times its previous valuation. Al Mada Ventures led the round, co-led by returning investor Silicon Badia, with Shorooq and Bunat Ventures increasing their investment and Du Ventures and Oraseya Capital joining as new investors. The funding will take Journify into the US and Europe and expand the AI behind its platform. Global ad spend will exceed $1 trillion in 2026, with algorithms expected to place three quarters by 2028, according to dentsu. These systems learn from the customer outcomes brands send back. Browser restrictions, broken tracking, and disconnected offline sales leave them with an incomplete picture of who buys. Journify makes sure ad platforms such as Google, Meta, TikTok, Snap and Amazon Ads see the purchases, sign-ups and store sales a brand’s customers actually make. More than 100 businesses use Journify today, from fast-growing ecommerce brands to some of the region’s largest retailers, representing hundreds of millions of dollars in annual ad spend. Customers include Jarir Bookstore, one of Saudi Arabia’s largest retailers, which increased its return on ad spend on Meta by 182%, and Saudi ecommerce brand Baytonia, which grew its return on ad spend on TikTok by 80% while cutting cost per purchase by 44%. “AI is transforming advertising, but the intelligence behind it is only as good as the signals it receives,” said Taoufik El Jamali, Co-Founder and CEO of Journify. “Businesses know who buys, who comes back and what creates lasting customer value. Too little of that knowledge reaches the ad platforms driving their growth. Our vision is to close that gap, turning real customer outcomes into intelligence ad platforms can learn from. title: What is FlashProve? Anthropic’s open-source tool to prove which AI model generated a response
summary: Anthropic has announced FlashProve, an open-source system for ‘provable inference’ that works like a cryptographic email signature for AI outputs. It aims to let users verify that a response came from the model a company claims to have, without exposing the model’s weights.

title: Schools are in control, Gemini and Search off by default: Google says amid controversy over Artificial Intelligence
summary: Google will turn off Gemini and other AI features by default for K-12 accounts and let schools enable them if they want to. The change follows criticism that Google pressured schools to adopt AI and might restrict search for those that refused to do so.
